title: First owner-recorded seizure event
description: Owner diary records an event lasting approximately 3-4 minutes before the morning walk, after Hope sniffed the lift. Owner states this first event was not reported to the veterinarian until after the 4 June events.

sourceDiscrepancy.clinicalRecordSummary: The 5 June clinical record describes the 28 May episode as lasting approximately 4-5 minutes with stiffened forelegs and drooling, followed by post-seizure confusion.
sourceDiscrepancy.resolution: Do not reconcile the duration. Preserve owner diary duration 3-4 minutes and clinic-note duration 4-5 minutes as separate source statements.

title: Owner-recorded seizure event during sleep
description: Owner diary records an event during sleep lasting approximately 2-3 minutes.

title: Second owner-recorded seizure event on 4 June
description: Owner diary records a second event during sleep on 4 June, lasting approximately 3-4 minutes.

title: Clinic note compresses owner-recorded seizure history
description: The 5 June Cornerstone note summarizes the pre-consultation history as two seizure episodes, while the owner diary contains three events before consultation: 28 May at 07:00 and 4 June at 01:00 and 05:00. The clinic note also gives the 28 May duration as 4-5 minutes whereas the owner diary records 3-4 minutes.

title: Idiopathic epilepsy suspected
description: Cornerstone Pet Clinic documented 'Idiopathic epilepsy suspected.' The clinical note itself summarizes the history as two seizure episodes; the owner diary separately documents three pre-consultation events.

title: Levetiracetam treatment documented
description: Epihat-LC (levetiracetam) 3.4 mL morning and night was documented as the initial antiseizure treatment.

title: Short-course adjunct seizure medications prescribed
description: Diamox and clonazepam were prescribed for 5 days alongside continued Epihat-LC.

title: Levetiracetam tablet formulation documented
description: LEVEPIL 500 mg prescription display states 0.7 tablet morning and night, while written instructions state three-quarter tablet every 8-12 hours. Owner confirms actual administration was 0.7 tablet morning and night.

title: Recurrent seizures documented
description: Telephonic clinical record documents recurrent seizures while levetiracetam and clonazepam were reported as current medications.

title: Phenobarbital prescribed
description: Gardenal 60 mg prescription display states 0.7 tablet morning and night for 10 days, while written instructions state three-quarter tablet twice daily. Owner confirms actual administration was 0.7 tablet morning and night.

title: Phenobarbital regimen documented
description: Gardenal 30 mg, two tablets morning and two tablets night, was prescribed for 10 days. Hepamust 7.5 mL morning and night was also prescribed for 10 days.

title: Animal Care review: medication continuation and obesity diet
description: Animal Care advised an obesity diet based on 17 kg body weight, review after one month, continuation of the same medication for one month, and daily Et Liv syrup. VetExpert Obesity food was prescribed. The same record contains 'ADVISE 2D ECHO FOR CURIE', which is treated as unrelated source contamination and is not attributed to Hope.

title: Serum phenobarbital below laboratory reference range
description: Serum phenobarbital result was 8.8 against the laboratory reference range 18-45 and the laboratory report labelled the result subtherapeutic.

title: Random/post-prandial bile acid reported normal
description: Bile acid result was 0.70 umol/L with laboratory reference <12 umol/L; the report states normal.

title: Current phenobarbital maintenance and rescue plan documented
description: Gardenal 60 mg was prescribed at one tablet twice daily after food, always. The record states Epihat three-quarter tablet SOS, clonazepam should be stopped, and Medazolam up to 1.9 mL intranasally in emergency using the clinic's original wording. Owner confirms current maintenance phenobarbital 60 mg one tablet morning and night, and actual SOS use of levetiracetam 500 mg three-quarter tablet.

sourceDiscrepancy.resolution: Preserve both statements without assuming the source line independently verifies the 500 mg strength.
